title: Day-in-the-Life Activity Library — Service + Technician Domains
scope: Service coordination, technician field work, Work Order lifecycle, scheduling and dispatch, equipment service context, inbound work intake, and the mobile and after-hours realities of field service at Taylor Freezer of Arizona (operating companies: taylor, ventana).
executionStatement: NOTHING IN THIS LIBRARY HAS BEEN EXECUTED. No activity was run against any real or production system. Every executionResult is NOT_RUN. No activity is labelled PASS, and an unexecuted activity may never be.

stories.title: Monday 06:40 - the weekend's email pile lands in the inbound queue
stories.primaryAccountContext: Mixed: Sonoran Scoops Creamery, QuikMart #418, Cactus Burger Co. #12
stories.narrative: Marisol opens the service mailbox queue before the phones start. Over the weekend the service@ mailbox took eleven messages: three genuine machine-down calls, a manufacturer recall notice, two 'just checking on my part', a spam invoice, one message from a Ventana-billed c-store chain that landed in the Taylor mailbox, and a resend of Friday's message whose original she already turned into a Work Order. Everything she does here decides whether a technician's Tuesday is real work or a wasted drive.

stories.title: 07:20 - the phone call that becomes a Work Order, and the number that must never repeat
stories.primaryAccountContext: Desert Ice & Cold Storage, 9100 W Buckeye Rd Tolleson - Vogt P24AL tube-ice machine
stories.narrative: Rosa takes a call from the plant manager at Desert Ice: the number-two Vogt is making half-size cubes and they are shipping to a grocery chain on Wednesday. She creates the Work Order by hand. This story exercises WO creation, numbering, the CREATED state, and what happens when the counter document behind woNumber is not in the state the code assumes.

stories.title: The machine on the Work Order - equipment context a technician can actually use
stories.primaryAccountContext: Sonoran Scoops Creamery - Tempe Mill Ave - Taylor C712 two-flavour soft-serve freezer
stories.narrative: Sonoran Scoops runs four stores. Three have Taylor C712s, one has an older C713 nobody updated in the register. Marisol links equipment to Work Orders all morning; Curtis reads the result on a phone in a parking lot. Everything wrong in the register becomes a wasted drive or a wrong part on the truck.

stories.title: 07:55 - Dale builds Tuesday on the dispatcher board
stories.primaryAccountContext: Mixed Taylor route: Cactus Burger #12, Sonoran Scoops Mill Ave, Camelback Convention Center
stories.narrative: Nine Work Orders sit in the Ready-to-Schedule queue. Dale has six technicians, one of whom is at a manufacturer training all day, and a convention centre that needs ice by 11:00. He places jobs on the technician-by-hour lane grid. Every placement is a governed Schedule transition, not a drag that becomes a fact.

stories.title: Blocked time - PTO, lunch, and the July 4th closure that cannot be recorded
stories.primaryAccountContext: n/a - internal workforce records, no customer account
stories.narrative: Priya records the shop's absences: Javier's Thursday PTO, the standing 12:00-12:30 lunch each technician carries, a manufacturer training block, a truck in for brakes, and the company holiday closure. The Owner ruled tonight that overlapping blocked-time facts are legitimate - unavailable time is the UNION of blocked intervals, never the sum and never prohibited. A COMPANY_CLOSURE may straddle a daily LUNCH. This story exists to test that ruling against what the code actually does.

stories.title: The recommendation that does not know about PTO
stories.primaryAccountContext: Mixed Taylor route
stories.narrative: The dispatcher board scores technicians for each unscheduled Work Order and shows the top recommendation on every queue card. Dale trusts it. This story tests whether the score deserves that trust, on a Thursday when Javier is on recorded PTO.

stories.title: 09:30 - the day changes: unschedule, reschedule, and the difference between them
stories.primaryAccountContext: Cactus Burger Co. #12, Sonoran Scoops Mill Ave, Camelback Convention Center
stories.narrative: A Taylor C602 at Cactus Burger goes fully down at 09:30 and jumps the queue. Dale has to take something off Curtis's afternoon. EOS gives him two different tools that look like one button: Unschedule, which is a lifecycle transition and the only reverse edge in the state machine, and Reschedule, which is a separate command that re-times a job without touching the lifecycle table at all.

stories.title: 10:10 - dispatching: committing a named technician to a named job
stories.primaryAccountContext: Cactus Burger Co. #12 (emergency), QuikMart #418, Rio Salado High School District
stories.narrative: Scheduling says when. Dispatch says go. The Dispatch action is the one that writes assignedTechId and starts the technician's half of the lifecycle, and it is the last point at which a dispatcher can change their mind cheaply.

stories.title: Who is this technician? - the two-hop identity join and the 13 that resolved to 0
stories.primaryAccountContext: n/a - identity and access, no customer account
stories.narrative: A technician's phone shows their jobs because users/{uid}.technicianId points at a fieldops_technicians record. Their truck's stock shows up because trucks.assignedDriverEmployeeId points at an employees record. These are two different id spaces, and joining them is where the day quietly breaks.

stories.title: 06:50 - Curtis starts his day: Accept, Travel, Arrive
stories.primaryAccountContext: QuikMart #418, 3900 W Indian School Rd Phoenix - Manitowoc IYT0500A ice machine
stories.narrative: Curtis reads his phone in his driveway with the truck idling. Four jobs are dispatched to him. The technician half of the lifecycle - Accept, Travel, Arrive, WorkStart, Complete - is the only part of the state machine he can drive, and every one of those actions requires that the job is HIS.

stories.title: 07:35 - arrival exceptions: the store is shut, the address is wrong, the machine is fine
stories.primaryAccountContext: QuikMart #418, Rio Salado High School District, Sonoran Scoops Chandler
stories.narrative: Half of a technician's exceptions happen in the first ninety seconds on site. The lifecycle gives him five verbs - Accept, Travel, Arrive, WorkStart, Complete - and none of them means 'I got here and I cannot do this'.

stories.title: 08:10 - the work itself: diagnosis, notes, and what a technician can record
stories.primaryAccountContext: QuikMart #418 - Manitowoc IYT0500A: low ice production, suspected condenser
stories.narrative: Curtis pulls the panel, finds a filthy condenser and a failing water inlet valve. What he can tell EOS about that is the difference between a service history and a pile of free text.

stories.title: 09:20 - parts off the truck: where did this actually come from?
stories.primaryAccountContext: QuikMart #418 - Manitowoc IYT0500A: water inlet valve and condenser kit
stories.narrative: Curtis fits a water inlet valve from the shelf behind his cab and a cleaning kit he picked up at the main warehouse yesterday. EOS must know which physical place each came from, because a part consumed from the wrong location moves the wrong on-hand balance and the error surfaces at a cycle count weeks later.

stories.title: 11:15 - a serialized compressor, and the row that counted twice
stories.primaryAccountContext: Sonoran Scoops Creamery - Tempe Mill Ave - Taylor C712: compressor replacement under warranty
stories.narrative: Javier replaces a compressor. A compressor is a SERIALIZED part - the company tracks the individual unit, not a quantity. Before Wave 1, the Work Order consumption write path hardcoded trackingMode = 'NONE' for everything it posted, and the read path took trackingMode off the callable REQUEST rather than from the part authority. This story exists to prove the fix holds and to catch its regression.

stories.title: 13:40 - the dead zone: queueing, syncing, and the conflict that comes back
stories.primaryAccountContext: Desert Ice & Cold Storage, Tolleson - a plant room with no signal
stories.narrative: Tonya spends ninety minutes inside a tube-ice plant with no signal, records four things, and comes back into coverage. The offline runtime is a durable local intent queue with a dependency graph, idempotency keys and failure classification - and no service worker, so it protects writes and not reads.

stories.title: 12:05 - completion, and the two people it takes to finish a Work Order
stories.primaryAccountContext: QuikMart #418 - Manitowoc IYT0500A, condenser cleaned and valve replaced
stories.narrative: Curtis finishes. Complete is the last action a technician may take; Close belongs to the office. The gap between them is where the invoice, the warranty claim and the customer's copy of the paperwork live - and it is a genuine handoff between two roles who cannot see each other's screens.

stories.title: The walls a technician hits, and the ones he should
stories.primaryAccountContext: Mixed - Taylor and Ventana jobs on shared technicians
stories.narrative: Some refusals protect the business. Some are accidents of an unmigrated access model. This story walks a technician into both kinds so an executor can tell them apart.

stories.title: Interruptions: back buttons, half-finished flows and the work that vanishes
stories.primaryAccountContext: Mixed
stories.narrative: A service coordinator is interrupted every four minutes and a technician every time a customer walks up. This story tests what survives an interruption in each of the domain's multi-step flows.

stories.title: 22:40 - the after-hours call: an ice plant down before a Wednesday delivery
stories.primaryAccountContext: Desert Ice & Cold Storage, Tolleson - Vogt P24AL #1 tripped and will not restart
stories.narrative: Ken carries the on-call phone. The plant manager calls at 22:40: the primary tube-ice machine is down and 40,000 lb of ice ships Wednesday morning. Everything Ken can do between 22:40 and midnight is constrained by a permission model designed around office hours, on a phone, with no dispatcher awake.

stories.title: The job that does not finish today - parts on order and the second visit
stories.primaryAccountContext: Sonoran Scoops Creamery - Chandler - Taylor C713: beater motor seized, part not stocked
stories.narrative: Half of all service calls in this business need a second visit. The lifecycle has eleven statuses and none of them means 'waiting for a part'. This story follows what a coordinator and a technician actually do with a job that cannot be finished.

stories.title: 14:20 - handing a job over: the transfer EOS cannot express
stories.primaryAccountContext: Camelback Convention Center - twin Manitowoc ice machines before a 2,000-cover banquet
stories.narrative: Curtis has been on a convention centre ice machine for three hours and has to leave for a school pickup. Javier finishes it. Every real service business does this daily, and the lifecycle has no verb for it.

stories.title: 17:20 - the dispatcher's end of day: what finished, what did not, what tomorrow inherits
stories.primaryAccountContext: Mixed Taylor and Ventana route
stories.narrative: Dale closes the board. Eleven jobs went out, seven completed, two are still in progress, one was cancelled and one never left DISPATCHED. Tomorrow's day is built from what is left, and the board has no notion of a day ending.

stories.title: The quarterly PM campaign - 62 convenience stores, one planning morning
stories.primaryAccountContext: QuikMart Southwest - 62 stores across Phoenix and Tucson, Manitowoc ice machines and FBD frozen-beverage units
stories.narrative: Preventive maintenance is the business's steadiest revenue and its worst data-entry experience. Rosa must create, schedule and dispatch preventive-maintenance Work Orders for 62 stores. Every governed action in this domain is a per-record command.

stories.title: Month end - closing the service month across two companies
stories.primaryAccountContext: All accounts, both operating companies
stories.narrative: The last working day of the month. Priya and Amanda must close the service month: every completed job closed, every open job explained, every number defensible. This story tests whether the service domain can produce a month.

stories.title: One customer, four machines, one trip - the coordinated visit
stories.primaryAccountContext: Sonoran Scoops Creamery - new Mesa store: two Taylor C712 freezers, one C302 shake machine, one Manitowoc ice machine, all from one Sales Order
stories.narrative: A new store opening puts four machines at one address on one day. EOS models this as four Work Orders that share a Sales Order and deliberately does NOT merge them into one record - each unit keeps its own lifecycle. The coordinated-visit surfaces exist to show the group without pretending it is a single job.

stories.title: Installing a machine at a customer - the irreversible act
stories.primaryAccountContext: Cactus Burger Co. #17, new store, Chandler - Taylor C602 shake machine from company inventory
stories.narrative: Installing a unit at a customer moves it permanently from company inventory to a customer's premises. The flow is confirm-before-permanent and idempotency-keyed, because doing it twice would create a second machine that does not exist.

stories.title: The mailbox behind the queue - inbound transport, credentials and the day it stops polling
stories.primaryAccountContext: service@ mailboxes for both operating companies
stories.narrative: Everything in the inbound work story assumes messages arrive. Behind the queue is a provider transport with credentials, a connection, a delivery schedule and a quarantine rule for unknown mailboxes. When it stops, the queue looks like a quiet day.

stories.title: The scorecard that refuses to lie
stories.primaryAccountContext: n/a - workforce performance, no customer account
stories.narrative: Curtis opens his performance page. Three of the four headline metrics show as visibly empty because they cannot honestly be computed from the data EOS holds. This story tests whether the honesty survives contact with a manager who wants numbers.

stories.title: Rosa's Ventana day on a shared account base
stories.primaryAccountContext: QuikMart Southwest, Tucson Gas & Go, Desert Ice & Cold Storage - Ventana-side service on accounts Taylor also serves
stories.narrative: Ventana and Taylor share one account base, one technician roster, one Work Order collection and one number series. Rosa spends her day working a company that the Work Order record does not know exists.

stories.title: The phone-call day - what a coordinator can find while a customer waits
stories.primaryAccountContext: Mixed - inbound phone calls across both companies
stories.narrative: Marisol takes about forty calls a day. Each one is a lookup race: find the account, find the machine, find the last visit, find the open job, answer the question. This story measures the domain by how fast a person can answer a customer who is standing next to a broken machine.

stories.title: A manufacturer safety notice - finding every affected machine in the field
stories.primaryAccountContext: All accounts holding Taylor C712 units in a serial range
stories.narrative: Taylor Company issues a service bulletin for a mix-pump seal on C712 units in a serial range. Priya must find every affected machine, get to each one, and prove afterwards that she did. This is the hardest read in the domain and the one with legal consequences.

stories.title: Cleanup Monday - putting right a week that went wrong
stories.primaryAccountContext: Mixed - the accumulated damage from this library's defects
stories.narrative: A week of the failures catalogued in this library has left the data in a state someone must now fix: duplicate Work Order numbers, jobs stuck in DISPATCHED, an unrecordable holiday, a truck join that resolves nothing, and parts recorded against warehouses nobody visited. This story tests whether EOS supports recovery at all.

stories.title: Day one - a new technician, and everything that must be true before he can work
stories.primaryAccountContext: n/a - onboarding, then first jobs at Cactus Burger Co. #12
stories.narrative: Wes Tanner starts on a Monday. Between a signed offer letter and his first tapped Accept lies a chain of records that must all be correct: a user, a role, a technician, a technicianId link, an employee, a truck, working availability. Any one of them missing produces a different kind of broken day.

activities.storyTitle: Monday 06:40 - the weekend's email pile lands in the inbound queue
activities.title: Open the inbound work queue and read the overnight backlog
activities.accountContext: Mixed: Sonoran Scoops Creamery, QuikMart #418, Cactus Burger Co. #12
activities.startingRecordsAndState: 11 inbound_work_requests: 8 AWAITING_DECISION, 2 NEEDS_REVIEW, 1 QUARANTINED. No Work Orders created yet from any of them.
activities.businessPurpose: Decide, before dispatch builds the day, which of the weekend's emails are real service demand.
preconditions: Marisol signed in as a Taylor service coordinator
Inbound email transport has polled and staged the weekend messages
At least one routing rule exists
activities.action: Navigate to the Inbound Work queue and sort by received time ascending.
activities.expectedEosStateTransition: None. Reading the queue changes no inbound_work_request status; AWAITING_DECISION and NEEDS_REVIEW are both still decidable (DECIDABLE_STATUSES).
activities.expectedAuthorityCapability: Read of the inbound work queue. The read service is a callable, not a client collection read.
activities.expectedUiResult: A list of 11 rows with sender, subject, normalized body preview, status chip, and routing classification.
activities.expectedAuditResult: No audit event. A read is not an event.
activities.expectedCrossObjectEffect: None.
activities.exceptionRecoveryBehaviour: If the transport has not polled, the queue is empty and indistinguishable from 'no weekend demand'. The screen must say when it last successfully polled, not just show zero rows.
activities.aiOpportunityNote: AI's value is classification/triage, not execution.
activities.helpOpportunity: An (i) on the status chip explaining the difference between AWAITING_DECISION and NEEDS_REVIEW - 'same queue, louder' is in the code comment and nowhere on screen.
activities.resetReplayNotes: Reset = delete the seeded inbound_work_requests and re-seed from a fixture of 11 provider messages. No WO side effects to unwind because nothing was decided.
defectsThisWouldCatch: An empty queue caused by a dead poller is presented identically to a genuinely quiet weekend.
activities.fullActivityBlockedReason: The activity is a persona acting through an application surface, which needs the app running against the Firestore emulator; the emulator hangs on the occupied port.
activities.coreAssertionNote: The activity's central domain claim can be asserted tonight as a `node --test` .mjs unit suite over pure modules, with no emulator and no browser.

activities.storyTitle: Monday 06:40 - the weekend's email pile lands in the inbound queue
activities.title: Accept a genuine machine-down email and let it create a Work Order
activities.accountContext: Cactus Burger Co. #12, 4400 N 24th St Phoenix - Taylor C602 shake machine
activities.startingRecordsAndState: inbound_work_request status AWAITING_DECISION, requestType SERVICE, resolved to account Cactus Burger Co. and location #12.
activities.businessPurpose: Turn a customer's 'our shake machine is blowing the breaker' email into governed service demand.
preconditions: The request is in a DECIDABLE status
Candidate account/location resolution produced exactly one match
activities.action: Click Accept, confirm the resolved account/location and the SERVICE_CALL type, submit.
activities.expectedEosStateTransition: inbound_work_request AWAITING_DECISION -> ACCEPTED, and a new Work Order is created in CREATED. Not READY_TO_DISPATCH - only the MarkReady action reaches that.
activities.expectedAuthorityCapability: workOrder.create. The accept path runs server-side and allocates the WO number inside the same transaction that writes the WO doc.
activities.expectedUiResult: Confirmation naming the new woNumber (WO-2026-0000NN) and a link to the Work Order.
activities.expectedAuditResult: Two staged audit events on the accept: 'accepted inbound request and created work order <woNumber>' and 'created work order <woNumber> from inbound request <id>'.
activities.expectedCrossObjectEffect: Work Order created; inbound request now carries workItemId and woNumber.
activities.exceptionRecoveryBehaviour: If the transaction fails mid-way neither the counter increment nor the WO doc commits, so no number is burned.
activities.aiOpportunityNote: AI's value is drafting text a human then approves.
activities.helpOpportunity: A 'why is this CREATED and not ready to dispatch?' explainer at the status chip on the resulting WO.
activities.resetReplayNotes: Replay-safe by design: the command is keyed and a second accept returns {replayed:true} with the same woNumber rather than a second WO.
activities.fullActivityBlockedReason: Exercises inbound mail intake, which needs both the Firestore emulator and a stubbed provider transport. The emulator hangs on the occupied port.
activities.coreAssertionNote: The activity's central domain claim can be asserted tonight as a `node --test` .mjs unit suite over pure modules, with no emulator and no browser.

activities.storyTitle: Monday 06:40 - the weekend's email pile lands in the inbound queue
activities.title: Press Accept twice because the first click seemed to hang
activities.accountContext: Cactus Burger Co. #12
activities.startingRecordsAndState: The same inbound_work_request as the previous activity; the first Accept has committed but the response has not reached the browser.
activities.businessPurpose: Prove that an impatient double-submit cannot mint two Work Orders for one customer email.
preconditions: The client has not yet rendered the result
activities.action: Click Accept a second time within a few seconds.
activities.expectedEosStateTransition: No second transition. The replay path finds the already-created Work Order and returns it.
activities.expectedAuthorityCapability: Same authority; idempotency is a property of the command, not of the caller.
activities.expectedUiResult: DESIRED: the UI should show the same confirmation with the same woNumber, and say plainly 'already accepted - this is the Work Order that was created'. Whether the current UI distinguishes replay from first-accept is UNPROVEN by this lane.
activities.expectedAuditResult: CURRENT: the replay path returns before staging a second pair of audit events, so history shows one acceptance, not two.
activities.expectedCrossObjectEffect: No second Work Order, no second woNumber allocated, no second counter increment.
activities.exceptionRecoveryBehaviour: If the UI silently renders the replayed result as if it were new, the coordinator learns nothing; if it errors, she may create a duplicate WO by hand instead.
activities.aiOpportunityNote: AI would be noise here; the task is already one deliberate act.
activities.helpOpportunity: A 'what happened?' line distinguishing 'created just now' from 'already created at 06:44 by you'.
activities.resetReplayNotes: No reset needed - this is the reset-safe path. To re-run, clear the request's workItemId.
defectsThisWouldCatch: A replayed accept rendered as a fresh success teaches coordinators that double-clicking is harmless, which is only true here.
activities.fullActivityBlockedReason: Exercises inbound mail intake, which needs both the Firestore emulator and a stubbed provider transport. The emulator hangs on the occupied port.
activities.coreAssertionNote: The activity's claim is about a surface, a Rules outcome, or stored data, and cannot be reduced to a pure-function assertion.

activities.title: Try to decide a request that a colleague already accepted while the page was open
activities.accountContext: Sonoran Scoops Creamery - Tempe Mill Ave
activities.startingRecordsAndState: The row still renders AWAITING_DECISION in Marisol's stale browser tab; the stored status is ACCEPTED.
activities.businessPurpose: Two coordinators work the same queue; the second one must not be able to double-decide.
preconditions: Another coordinator accepted the request after this page loaded
activities.action: Click Decline on the stale row.
activities.expectedEosStateTransition: No transition. ACCEPTED is not in DECIDABLE_STATUSES, so the command refuses.
activities.expectedAuthorityCapability: Authority is present; the refusal is a state guard, not a permission failure. The UI must not blame the user's role.
activities.expectedUiResult: DESIRED: 'This request was accepted by Dale Brackett at 06:51 and became WO-2026-000141.' CURRENT wording is UNPROVEN by this lane.
activities.expectedAuditResult: A refused command should leave no state-change event. Whether refusals are themselves audited is UNPROVEN.
activities.expectedCrossObjectEffect: None.
activities.exceptionRecoveryBehaviour: The row must refresh in place to the real status rather than leaving the coordinator staring at a status the server disagrees with.
activities.aiOpportunityNote: AI's value is explaining a refusal or a state, not changing it.
activities.helpOpportunity: 'Who decided this, and what did it become?' is the question, and there is no obvious place on the row to answer it.
activities.resetReplayNotes: Seed two sessions; reset by restoring the request to AWAITING_DECISION.

activities.title: Find the duplicate resend of Friday's message already marked DUPLICATE
